# Results — Study 429 (Mass Index, Donald Dorsey)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **when the
Mass Index "bulges" above 27 and falls back below 26.5, a trend reversal is imminent** — tested
two ways on the real daily tape. **(1) Event study:** treat each completed bulge as an event and
measure the **forward 5 / 10 / 20 / 40-day return** after it, against the **unconditional base
rate**, both raw and **signed against the prevailing trend** (a genuine reversal makes the
trend-fade pay). **(2) Timing rule:** turn the bulge into a daily **post-bulge fade** and race it
**NET** of one-way costs × NAV against **buy-and-hold**, excess-of-cash to excess-of-cash, with a
one-day execution lag. As-of **2026-06-23** (the partial 2026-06-24 bar is dropped). Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **OHLCV**, auto-adjusted (total-return proxy) — SPY (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-06-23** (the partial 2026-06-24 session is dropped) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-23 (**21.4** years; **5,401** sessions) |
| Fingerprint (SPY close) | `aec1923d846c` |
| Indicator | Dorsey **Mass Index**: 25-day sum of EMA₉(range) / EMA₉(EMA₉(range)) |
| Bulge rule | Mass Index rises **> 27**, then falls back **< 26.5** — fires on the completing bar |
| Bulges fired | **36** completed bulges over 21.4 years (~1.7/yr) |
| Lag / costs | signal at close *t*, forward window / position over *t+1* (one shift); **1 bp** one-way × NAV; 50 bps/yr borrow on any short leg |
| Robustness panel | SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD (same window) |

## The event study — what actually happens after a bulge (raw forward return)

For each of the 36 bulges, the forward H-day simple return entered one day later, vs the
unconditional base rate over the same tape. The *t* is a one-sample *t* of the bulge sample vs 0;
*t-vs-base* is a Welch *t* of the bulge sample against the non-bulge sample; the placebo *p* is the
share of 5,000 random equal-size trigger sets whose |mean forward return| beats the observed one.

| horizon | n bulges | bulge mean | base-rate mean | win-rate | one-sample *t* | *t* vs base | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 36 | +0.15% | +0.24% | 64% | +0.32 | −0.20 | 0.757 |
| 10-day | 36 | −0.49% | +0.47% | 58% | −0.70 | −1.38 | 0.531 |
| 20-day | 36 | +0.07% | +0.94% | 67% | +0.06 | −0.76 | 0.968 |
| 40-day | 36 | +2.51% | +1.86% | 69% | +2.30 | +0.59 | 0.269 |

Read it carefully. The post-bulge return is **indistinguishable from the base rate** at every
horizon — in fact the bulge sample **trails** the unconditional mean at 5/10/20 days (the *t* vs
base is *negative*). The lone "significant" cell, 40-day one-sample *t* = +2.30, is a **mirage of
the base rate**: the market simply drifts up over 40 days (base +1.86%), and the bulge mean
(+2.51%) is not reliably above it (*t* vs base = +0.59, placebo *p* = 0.27). A bulge tells you
nothing the calendar didn't.

## The directional test — does the bulge call a *reversal*?

A reversal claim is directional, so we sign the forward return **against the prevailing trend** at
the bulge (`−trend_sign × forward return`): a true reversal after a bulge makes "fade the trend"
positive; a continuation makes it negative.

| horizon | fade mean | base (fade) | win-rate | one-sample *t* | *t* vs base | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | +0.84% | −0.05% | 53% | **+1.95** | +2.06 | 0.039 |
| 10-day | +0.85% | −0.10% | 47% | +1.25 | +1.39 | 0.116 |
| 20-day | +1.59% | −0.10% | 56% | +1.42 | +1.50 | 0.039 |
| 40-day | +0.34% | −0.18% | 53% | +0.29 | +0.44 | 0.761 |

There's a *whiff* here — the fade is positive at every horizon and the 5-day *t* reaches **+1.95**
— but it **never clears the desk's t ≥ 2 bar** on the real tape, the win-rate hovers near a coin
flip (47–56%), and the effect is non-monotone (it fades out by 40 days). On a 36-event sample this
is exactly the "interesting but not certified" pattern the inference bar is written to catch. The
literature's reversal claim is *suggestive* on this tape, not *real*: **WEAK at best, and we stamp
the Signal NONE** because it does not clear the bar and reverses sign across the panel (below).

## The timing rule — fade after a bulge, NET vs buy-and-hold

Turn the bulge into a daily rule: on a completing bulge, take the trend-fade exposure for the next
20 days, otherwise stay long. Excess-vs-excess Sharpe, NET 1 bp one-way × NAV, one-day lag.

| Rule | net Sharpe | CAGR | max drawdown | time-in-mkt | turnover/yr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Buy-and-hold | **+0.637** | +10.8% | −55.2% | 100% | — |
| **Post-bulge fade (long/flat, hold 20)** | **+0.754** | +12.2% | −48.5% | 90% | 2.5 |

The fade rule's Sharpe (**+0.75**) edges buy-and-hold (**+0.64**), but the **HAC *t* of the daily
(fade − buy-hold) difference is only +0.67** — nowhere near significant. The reason is mundane: a
bulge fires ~1.7×/yr and the rule is in the market **90%** of the time, so it is essentially
buy-and-hold with an occasional 20-day defensive tilt that happened, over this sample, to dodge a
couple of bad stretches. There is no separable, repeatable edge — the *t* says so.

## Timing variants & cost sweep — nothing is significant, costs barely matter

| Variant | net Sharpe | HAC *t* vs buy-hold |
|---|--:|--:|
| hold 10, long/flat | +0.711 | +1.01 |
| hold 10, long/short | +0.745 | +1.00 |
| **hold 20, long/flat** | **+0.754** | **+0.67** |
| hold 20, long/short | +0.735 | +0.66 |
| hold 40, long/flat | +0.657 | −0.82 |
| hold 40, long/short | +0.461 | −0.84 |

| one-way cost | net Sharpe | HAC *t* vs buy-hold |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +0.755 | +0.69 |
| 1.0 bps | +0.754 | +0.67 |
| 2.0 bps | +0.753 | +0.66 |
| 5.0 bps | +0.748 | +0.60 |

No variant clears HAC *t* = 2; the longer 40-day fade actively *hurts* (it stays defensive through
up-legs). Because the rule barely trades (~2.5 round-trips/yr), costs are almost irrelevant — which
only underscores that there's no edge for costs to eat.

## The panel — the sign of the "reversal" is not stable

Fade event-study (h = 20) and the timing race across five ETFs:

| Ticker | n bulges | fade@20 mean | one-sample *t* | timing Sharpe | buy-hold Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 36 | +1.59% | +1.42 | +0.754 | +0.637 | +0.67 |
| QQQ | 29 | **−0.62%** | −0.48 | +0.834 | +0.768 | +0.27 |
| IWM | 19 | +0.73% | +0.34 | +0.536 | +0.473 | +0.88 |
| DIA | 31 | +0.63% | +0.57 | +0.738 | +0.619 | +0.56 |
| GLD | 23 | **−1.24%** | −0.97 | +0.600 | +0.648 | −1.34 |

The post-bulge fade is **positive on three tapes and negative on two** (QQQ, GLD), and clears no
*t* anywhere. A real reversal effect would point the same way across markets; this flips sign — the
classic signature of a small-sample artefact, not a signal.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel that plants a **real** post-bulge reversal (each engineered range-bulge is
preceded by a trend that then *flips* for ~25 days; knob `edge`), the same detector + fade engine
behaves exactly as it must:

| planted edge | bulges detected | fade@20 mean | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | timing Sharpe | buy-hold Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.0** (no reversal) | 57 | −0.45% | −0.50 | 0.930 | +0.257 | +0.364 | −0.85 |
| **3.0** (real reversal) | 79 | **+16.68%** | **+3.94** | **0.000** | **+2.787** | +0.258 | **+4.74** |

With **no** planted reversal the fade sits at *t* ≈ 0 (placebo *p* = 0.93 — no false positive); with
a genuine planted reversal it lights up massively (*t* = +3.94, timing Sharpe +2.79 vs +0.26,
HAC *t* = +4.74). The harness *can* detect a post-bulge reversal when one is really there — so the
flat real-tape result is a **true negative**, not a broken pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The raw post-bulge return matches the base rate at every horizon (the bulge
  sample even *trails* it at 5/10/20 days; the lone 40-day *t* = 2.30 is the calendar drift, *t* vs
  base only +0.59). The directional trend-fade is suggestive (5-day *t* = **+1.95**) but **never
  clears the desk's t ≥ 2 bar** on the real tape, sits near a coin-flip win-rate, and **flips sign
  across the panel** (QQQ −0.62%, GLD −1.24%). Literature says "reversal"; this tape can't certify
  it. NONE, not WEAK.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The post-bulge fade scores Sharpe **+0.75** vs buy-and-hold **+0.64**,
  but HAC *t* of the daily difference is only **+0.67** — insignificant. The rule is long 90% of the
  time and trades ~2.5×/yr, so it is buy-and-hold with an occasional defensive tilt; no variant
  clears significance and costs barely move it. Nothing separable to deploy.
- **"The range bulge calls a reversal"? — BUSTED.** The Mass Index bulge is **volatility
  clustering**, not a reversal oracle: the forward return after a bulge is statistically
  indistinguishable from the base rate, the directional version doesn't clear the bar, and its sign
  isn't even stable across markets — while the synthetic control proves the harness *would* have
  caught a real post-bulge reversal had one existed.
